title: Build Monday's call list
prompt:
Marketing can call 20 customers. Give them the right 20.

1. `model`: a pipeline of `StandardScaler` then `LogisticRegression`, fitted on the training data.
2. `churn_prob`: the churn probability (class 1) for each test customer.
3. `call_list`: the `customer_id` values of the 20 test customers with the highest churn probability.
4. `hit_rate`: the share of those 20 who actually churned.
hints: `predict` gives labels. `predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]` gives the churn column of probabilities.
`X_test` keeps the original row index, so `churn.loc[X_test.index, "customer_id"]` lines up with `churn_prob`. Add the probabilities as a column, sort descending, take `head(20)`.
explanation: Ranking by probability concentrates the call budget: well over 80% of the 20 riskiest test customers really churned, against 55% for a random pick. `predict` would only have said "1" for dozens of customers without any order among them. Keeping the original index from `train_test_split` is what lets you join predictions back to ids.

checks.call-list: call_list has the 20 highest-risk customer ids
checks.hit-rate: hit_rate is the share of the call list who churned
